# CSV review-fix evidence

The actual CLI received 10,000 rows (`name,value` header, `example,12345` rows).
A Python pipe consumer read eight lines and closed stdout, like `head -n 8`.
The producer returned exit 0 and wrote no stderr. The permanent Rust regression
uses a stricter consumer that closes after one byte; it failed before this fix.

`csv-head.txt` is the actual eight-line output. `csv-head.svg` is generated by
`rich csv-head.txt --export-svg csv-head.svg` with COLUMNS=48 and TERM=xterm-256color.
The JPG is a browser screenshot of that CLI export, without image editing.

Validation: workspace default/all-feature tests, CLI no-default tests, all-target
all-feature Clippy, formatting, Rust 1.90 check and strict documentation build.
Feature configurations were checked sequentially; a fresh default target was
used to avoid stale executable reuse between configurations in the shared target.
The independent reviewer repeated the closed-pipe experiment successfully.
